mainTopic: שמואל הקטן and ברכת המינים; the number of ברכות on special days; the shortened תפילה הביננו and when it may be said
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of שמואל הקטן, who forgot ברכת המינים while leading the prayer and still was not removed. The גמרא asks why, since רב rules that someone who skips this ברכה is removed. First it says the author of the ברכה is above suspicion, and אביי adds that a truly good person does not turn bad. After challenges from a פסוק and from the story of יוחנן כהן גדול, and רבא's view that anyone can fall, the final answer is that שמואל הקטן had already begun the ברכה. The גמרא then gives sources for the number of ברכות on שבת (seven), ראש השנה (nine) and a תענית (twenty-four). Next it explains רבי יהושע's shortened תפילה: רב says each ברכה is shortened, while שמואל gives the single ברכה of הביננו. It discusses when הביננו may not be said: on מוצאי שבת because of הבדלה, and in the rainy season because of the request for rain. Finally it examines רב אסי's rule about forgetting rain or הבדלה, faces a contradicting ברייתא, and begins an answer that finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן forgets the blessing but stays at his post
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן spent two or three hours trying to remember ברכת המינים, and they did not remove him from leading the prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he gazed into it for two or three hours, and they did not remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story: שמואל הקטן was leading the prayer, forgot ברכת המינים, and stood there for a long time trying to recall it. The people did not replace him, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that matters is the end: 'they did not remove him.' Normally a שליח ציבור who skips this specific ברכה is removed, so this ending is surprising. The next step will point that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Gazed, looked into. Here it means he thought hard trying to remember.
They brought him up, meaning they removed him from leading the prayer.
The חכם who composed ברכת המינים.

phrases.english: And he gazed into it
phrases.notes: 'It' is ברכת המינים, the ברכה he forgot. He was straining to remember the words.

phrases.english: for two or three hours,
and they did not remove him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun before this section about שמואל הקטן forgetting ברכת המינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although שמואל הקטן forgot ברכת המינים, he was not removed as שליח ציבור.

steps.title: רב's rule says he should have been removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל הקטן was not removed, since רב rules that someone who errs in ברכת המינים is removed because he may be a מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they not remove him? Didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: If he erred in any of the blessings, we do not remove him; but in ברכת המינים, we remove him, because we suspect he may be a heretic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story using a ruling of רב, which seems to require removing a leader who skips ברכת המינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mistakes in most ברכות are innocent, so the leader stays. ברכת המינים is a curse against heretics, and a heretic would avoid saying it on purpose. Skipping it therefore raises suspicion, so why was שמואל הקטן left in place?

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
But didn't (he) say? This introduces a source that contradicts what we just saw.
The ברכה in שמונה עשרה against heretics.
We are concerned or suspect.
A heretic.

phrases.english: Why did they not remove him?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
If he erred in any of the blessings at all,
we do not remove him;
in the blessing of the heretics, we remove him.
We suspect that perhaps he is a heretic!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי לֹא הֶעֱלוּהוּ? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ending of the story in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that they did not remove שמואל הקטן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that someone who errs in ברכת המינים is removed out of suspicion of heresy, so שמואל הקטן should have been removed.

steps.title: The author of the blessing is beyond suspicion
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן is different because he himself composed ברכת המינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן is different, because he is the one who composed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's rule does not apply to שמואל הקטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule rests on suspicion. The man who wrote the curse against heretics is clearly not trying to avoid it, so his forgetting was an honest mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. This marks an exception to a rule.
He composed or established it.

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan is different,
for he himself instituted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the suspicion behind the rule does not exist here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule applies to every שליח ציבור who skips ברכת המינים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is based on suspicion, and the author of the ברכה is not suspected.

steps.title: Maybe he changed his ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we should still worry that שמואל הקטן changed and became a heretic.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps he changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Writing the ברכה long ago doesn't prove he is still loyal today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 relied on his past. The challenge asks why that past should guarantee the present, since people can change.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be concerned.
Perhaps.
He went back on it, changed his mind.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he reconsidered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל הקטן is above suspicion because he composed the ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person who was once righteous might have changed, so the suspicion could still apply.

steps.title: A good person does not turn bad
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a tradition: someone who is truly good does not become wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that a good person does not become bad.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a received tradition, so there is no need to suspect שמואל הקטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that he might have changed. אביי says that a person who is truly good does not fall into wickedness, so שמואל הקטן's past goodness does protect him from suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it as a tradition.
A good person.
A bad or wicked person.

steps.whatToRemember: Skipping ברכת המינים normally gets a שליח ציבור removed out of suspicion. The first answer for שמואל הקטן is that he wrote the ברכה, and אביי adds that a truly good person does not become wicked. The next steps test this, and step 14 gives the answer that works even for רבא: he had already begun the ברכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We have learned by tradition:
A good person does not become bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Received tradition (גמירי) that removes the concern.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even a righteous person might change, so שמואל הקטן could be suspected.
steps.terutzMaskana: A truly good person does not become wicked, so there is no suspicion.

steps.title: A verse says a righteous person can turn to sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's rule using a פסוק that talks about a צדיק who turns away from his righteousness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he can't become wicked? But it is written: 'And when a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does wrong.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's rule that a truly good person never turns bad. It quotes a פסוק that clearly describes a צדיק who goes bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a צדיק does not become a רשע. The פסוק in יחזקאל openly describes a צדיק who leaves his righteousness and does evil. So the תורה itself seems to say it can happen.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And not?!' A surprised challenge: 'Is that really so?'
'But isn't it written...' This brings a פסוק as a challenge.
A righteous person
Wrongdoing, evil

phrases.english: And he doesn't [become wicked]?!
But isn't it written: 'And when a righteous person turns away from his righteousness
and does wrong.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's tradition from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a truly good person does not become wicked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly describes a צדיק who turns to evil, so it can happen.

steps.title: The verse is about someone who was wicked from the start
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is talking about a person who was a רשע at first and later did תשובה. Someone who was righteous from the start does not turn bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is about someone who was wicked from the beginning. But someone who was righteous from the beginning does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer narrows the פסוק. It is about a person who began as a רשע, became good, and then slid back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits 'righteous' people into two kinds. A צדיק מעיקרו, good from the start, does not fall. A former רשע who became good can slide back, and that is the person the פסוק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: Wicked from the start; a person who was originally a sinner
Righteous from the start; good all along
'That one', meaning that verse or that case

phrases.english: That [verse is about] someone wicked from the start,
but someone righteous from the start does not [become wicked].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the verse is about a different kind of person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show that any צדיק can turn wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who was originally a רשע can slide back. A צדיק מעיקרו does not.

steps.title: The story of יוחנן כהן גדול who became a צדוקי
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches not to trust yourself until you die, because יוחנן כהן גדול served eighty years and then became a צדוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he can't become wicked? But we learned in a משנה: Do not trust yourself until the day you die, for יוחנן the כהן גדול served as כהן גדול for eighty years and in the end became a צדוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, this time from a משנה. It tells of a man who seemed good for eighty years and still became a heretic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eighty years of service as כהן גדול seems to describe a person who was good from the start. If even he became a צדוקי, then a צדיק מעיקרו can also fall. That would break the answer of step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't we learn in a משנה...' This brings a משנה as a challenge.
Don't trust yourself, meaning don't be sure you will stay good
The office of כהן גדול
A Sadducee, a member of a group that rejected the Oral תורה

phrases.english: And he doesn't?! But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ,
phrases.english: Do not trust yourself until the day you die,
for Yochanan the High Priest
served as High Priest for eighty years
and in the end became a Sadducee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the answer of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a צדיק מעיקרו does not become wicked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוחנן seemed righteous from the start, since he served eighty years, yet he became a צדוקי.

steps.title: אביי: יוחנן and ינאי are the same
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that יוחנן is the same as ינאי, a known רשע. So יוחנן was never truly a צדיק מעיקרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: ינאי is יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his rule. The יוחנן in the משנה is the same as ינאי, who was wicked all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יוחנן and ינאי are one, then יוחנן was a רשע מעיקרו from the start. So his becoming a צדוקי does not show that a real צדיק can fall, and אביי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: King ינאי, known in the גמרא as a wicked ruler who opposed the חכמים
'He is... he is', meaning these are one and the same

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He is Yannai, he is Yochanan.
phrases.notes: אביי means you can't separate them. יוחנן was really the same wicked type as ינאי all along.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוּא יַנַּאי, הוּא יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the person in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יוחנן seemed to be a צדיק מעיקרו who fell.
steps.terutzMaskana: יוחנן was a רשע מעיקרו, the same as ינאי, so the rule stands.

steps.title: רבא: ינאי and יוחנן are different people
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. He says ינאי was wicked from the start, but יוחנן was righteous from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: ינאי is separate and יוחנן is separate. ינאי was wicked from the start, and יוחנן was righteous from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another view of the story. In his view יוחנן truly began as a צדיק. This sets up the next difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not accept that יוחנן was the same as ינאי. For him יוחנן really was a צדיק מעיקרו who later became a צדוקי. That clashes with the rule that such a person never falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Separately; a different thing
An אמורא who often disagrees with אביי

phrases.english: Rava said:
Yannai is separate and Yochanan is separate,
Yannai was wicked from the start,
and Yochanan was righteous from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: יַנַּאי לְחוּד וְיוֹחָנָן לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's identification in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוחנן was a צדיק מעיקרו, unlike ינאי who was a רשע מעיקרו.

steps.title: The משנה fits אביי but is hard for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's view fits the rule, but רבא's view runs into the problem of a צדיק מעיקרו who fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for אביי, but for רבא it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the problem with רבא's view. If יוחנן was a true צדיק and still fell, the rule from step 7 seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי there is no problem, since יוחנן was always wicked. For רבא, יוחנן is proof that a צדיק מעיקרו can turn bad. So the difficulty now falls only on רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works out fine' for one opinion
'But... it is difficult' for the other opinion

phrases.english: It works out well for Abaye,
but for Rava it is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the problem that step 10 creates
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that יוחנן was a צדיק מעיקרו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יוחנן was righteous from the start and still fell, the rule that a צדיק מעיקרו does not fall is broken.

steps.title: רבא: even a lifelong צדיק might change
steps.stepSummary: רבא would say that even someone righteous from the start might go bad. He does not accept the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would tell you: Even someone righteous from the start might change his ways.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers simply by not accepting the rule. In his view, anyone can fall, even a צדיק מעיקרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gives up the claim that a צדיק מעיקרו is safe. יוחנן proves that such a person can turn bad. This saves רבא from the difficulty, but it brings back the question about שמואל הקטן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He would tell you', meaning how this opinion would answer
Perhaps; maybe
Changed his mind; turned back from his ways

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
Even someone righteous from the start
might perhaps change his ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's answer to the difficulty in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge and dropping the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agreed that a צדיק מעיקרו never falls.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, even a צדיק מעיקרו may fall.

steps.title: Then why wasn't שמואל הקטן removed?
steps.stepSummary: If even a lifelong צדיק might turn bad, the old question comes back: why didn't they remove שמואל הקטן?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why didn't they remove him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening story. If anyone can fall, שמואל הקטן should have been removed when he stumbled in ברכת המינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא there is no promise that a צדיק stays good. So the worry from step 4, that שמואל הקטן may have changed, is back. The question from step 2 returns, and step 14 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so', meaning if that is true
Why?
'They removed him', taking him down from leading the תפילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one answer can bring back an older question. Dropping the rule to save רבא reopens the original problem about שמואל הקטן.

phrases.english: If so,
why didn't they remove him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is שמואל הקטן from the start of the story, who forgot ברכת המינים while leading the prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's answer from step 12 to reopen the original question
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that שמואל הקטן was not removed (step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a צדיק מעיקרו may turn bad, the worry that שמואל הקטן became a מין still applies, so רב's rule should have removed him.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן had already started the blessing
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן is different because he had already begun ברכת המינים before he got stuck.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן's case is different, because he had already begun the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. שמואל הקטן was not removed because he had already started ברכת המינים before he forgot it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about removing a שליח ציבור is aimed at someone who skips ברכת המינים completely, because that looks suspicious. שמואל הקטן began it and only lost his place partway through. So the rule never applied to him, and we do not need to worry that he went bad.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Since he had begun it
The blessing against heretics in the weekday שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan is different
since he had begun it.
phrases.notes: "It" means ברכת המינים, the blessing he forgot partway through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 13 without needing אביי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: started the blessing vs. skipped it entirely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל הקטן was a normal case of someone who erred in ברכת המינים, so he should have been removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had started the blessing, so the removal rule does not apply to him at all.

steps.title: Someone who began the blessing may finish it
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב (or רבי יהושע בן לוי): the removal rule applies only when he did not begin the blessing. If he began, he finishes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי said: They only taught this when he did not begin it. But if he began it, he finishes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a known teaching. The removal rule only applies to someone who never started ברכת המינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching shows that the line drawn in step 14 is an accepted rule, not a new idea made up to answer the question. If he started the blessing, we let him collect his thoughts and finish it instead of removing him.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was another רב who said it)
They only taught this when...
He finishes it

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who skips ברכת המינים is removed. Someone who started it and got stuck is allowed to finish. That is why שמואל הקטן stayed.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל בָּהּ,
phrases.english: They only taught this where he did not begin it,
but if he began it, he finishes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the distinction used in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between beginning ברכת המינים and not beginning it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב / רבי יהושע בן לוי

steps.title: What do the seven blessings of שבת match?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the seven ברכות of the שבת תפילה correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: These seven blessings of שבת, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Earlier it explained what the nineteen weekday ברכות match, and now it asks the same about the seven ברכות of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the weekday number was tied to a source, the גמרא assumes the שבת number also has a basis. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to what?
The seven blessings of שבת

phrases.english: These seven of Shabbat, corresponding to what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, parallel to the earlier discussion of the nineteen weekday ברכות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the number seven in the שבת תפילה

steps.title: The seven voices David mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלפתא בן שאול: they match the seven times דוד said "קול" over the waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלפתא בן שאול said: They correspond to the seven "voices" that דוד said over the waters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלפתא בן שאול answers the question. The seven ברכות of שבת match the seven times the word "voice" appears in דוד's psalm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same psalm in תהלים was used earlier as a source for the weekday ברכות. Here the seven mentions of "voice of ה׳" give the number seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Voices ("the voice of ה׳")
Over the waters

phrases.english: Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul said:
Corresponding to the seven "voices"
that David said over the waters.
phrases.notes: תהלים 29, where "the voice of ה׳ is over the waters" opens the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.

steps.title: What do the nine blessings of ראש השנה match?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the nine ברכות of the ראש השנה מוסף correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: These nine blessings of ראש השנה, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about the nine ברכות of ראש השנה. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש השנה מוסף has nine ברכות because of the three extra sections. The גמרא looks for a source for that number.

keyTerms.meaning: The nine blessings of ראש השנה

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תֵּשַׁע דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּנֶגֶד מִי?
phrases.english: These nine of Rosh HaShana, corresponding to what?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תֵּשַׁע דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of question, now for ראש השנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the number nine in the ראש השנה תפילה

steps.title: The nine mentions of ה׳'s name in חנה's prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דמן קרטיגנין: they match the nine times חנה mentioned ה׳'s name in her prayer. This fits because חנה was remembered on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק of קרטיגנין said: They correspond to the nine mentions of ה׳'s name that חנה said in her prayer. As the Master said: On ראש השנה, שרה, רחל and חנה were remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק says the nine ברכות match the nine times חנה said ה׳'s name in her prayer. The גמרא then explains why חנה is connected to ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would חנה's prayer be the model for ראש השנה? Because a known teaching says ה׳ remembered חנה, and granted her a child, on ראש השנה. So her prayer is naturally linked to that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentions of ה׳'s name
As the Master said (quoting a known teaching)
Was remembered (granted a child)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of Kartignin said:
Corresponding to the nine mentions of God's name
that Chana said in her prayer,
phrases.notes: Her prayer of thanks in שמואל א 2:1–10.

phrases.english: as the Master said: On Rosh HaShana
Sarah, Rachel and Chana were remembered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 and gives the link between חנה and ראש השנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nine אזכרות in חנה's prayer, linked to ראש השנה because she was remembered on that day

steps.title: What do the twenty-four blessings of a fast day match?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the twenty-four ברכות said on a תענית correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: These twenty-four blessings of a fast day, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question a third time, now about the twenty-four ברכות said on a public fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a special תענית, extra ברכות are added, bringing the total to twenty-four. The גמרא wants the source for that number.

keyTerms.meaning: A fast day
Twenty-four

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע דְּתַעֲנִיתָא כְּנֶגֶד מִי?
phrases.english: These twenty-four of a fast day, corresponding to what?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע דְּתַעֲנִיתָא כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of question, now for a תענית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the number twenty-four in the fast-day תפילה

steps.title: The twenty-four songs of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו: they match the twenty-four expressions of song and prayer שלמה said when he brought the ארון into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: They correspond to the twenty-four "songs" that שלמה said when he brought the ארון into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו answers that the twenty-four ברכות match the twenty-four words of song and prayer in שלמה's prayer at the dedication of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה's prayer at that moment uses words of song, prayer and pleading twenty-four times. Those are the model for the twenty-four fast-day ברכות. This answer sets up a challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Songs (expressions of song and prayer)
The Holy of Holies
The Ark

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
Corresponding to the twenty-four "songs"
that Shlomo said at the time
when he brought the Ark into the Holy of Holies:
phrases.notes: מלכים א פרק 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The twenty-four רננות of שלמה at the dedication of the בית המקדש

steps.title: Then say them every day
steps.stepSummary: If the twenty-four come from שלמה's prayer, why not say them every day?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should say them every day too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חלבו. If the source is שלמה's prayer, nothing in it seems tied to fast days, so why not say all twenty-four every day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weak point is that רבי חלבו's source does not explain why these ברכות are limited to a תענית. The challenge pushes him to explain that limit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Every day

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי נֵמְרִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: If so, let us say them every day too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי נֵמְרִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חלבו's source for the twenty-four ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is not tied to fast days, so it should apply every day.

steps.title: שלמה said them on a day of asking for mercy
steps.stepSummary: שלמה said them on a day of pleading for mercy, so we also say them only on such a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did שלמה say them? On a day of asking for mercy. We too say them on a day of asking for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the timing of שלמה's prayer matters. He said it on a day of pleading for mercy, so we copy him on a fast day, which is also a day of pleading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source gives both the number and the kind of day. Because שלמה was pleading for mercy, the twenty-four ברכות belong to a day like a תענית, not to an ordinary day.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
A day of asking for mercy

steps.whatToRemember: Seven for שבת (דוד's seven voices), nine for ראש השנה (חנה's nine mentions of ה׳), twenty-four for a תענית (שלמה's twenty-four songs, said on a day of mercy).

phrases.english: When did Shlomo say them?
On a day of asking for mercy,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן נָמֵי בְּיוֹמָא דְרַחֲמֵי אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ.
phrases.english: so we too say them on a day of asking for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following the source's setting: the occasion of the prayer limits when it is said
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the source is שלמה's prayer, the twenty-four should be said daily.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה said them on a day of pleading for mercy, so we say them only on such days, like a תענית.

steps.title: What does a shortened שמונה עשרה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע from the משנה and asks what he means by a shortened version of שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: one says a shortened version of the eighteen blessings. What is this shortened version?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up the answers of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allows a shorter תפילה, but he doesn't say how short or in what form. The גמרא wants to know what this short version actually sounds like.

keyTerms.meaning: A summary or shortened form of something
The eighteen blessings of the עמידה
What is it?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A shortened version of the eighteen.
What is "a shortened version of the eighteen"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה after finishing the discussion of how many ברכות are said on special days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the shortened form of שמונה עשרה that רבי יהושע allows?

steps.title: רב: shorten every single blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב says the shortened version means saying a short form of each one of the blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a short form of each and every blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. You still go through every blessing, but each one is said in a short form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, all eighteen blessings stay as separate blessings. Only the length of each one is cut down.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every blessing

phrases.english: Rav said:
A shortened version of each and every blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מֵעֵין כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each blessing is said in a short form, keeping all of them.

steps.title: שמואל: the הביננו blessing
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the shortened version is one special blessing, הביננו, that sums up all the middle requests, and he gives its full wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: "Give us understanding, ה׳ our God, to know Your ways; soften our hearts to fear You; forgive us so we can be redeemed; keep us far from our pains; fill us from the good pastures of Your land; gather our scattered people from the four corners; let those who stray be judged by Your will; raise Your hand against the wicked; let the righteous rejoice in the rebuilding of Your city and the repair of Your Temple, in the growing strength of Your servant דוד and the lamp set up for the son of ישי, Your anointed one. Before we call, may You answer. Blessed are You ה׳, Who hears prayer."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer. Instead of shortening each blessing, you say one blessing that sums up all the middle requests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line of הביננו points to one of the middle blessings: knowledge, repentance, forgiveness, redemption, healing, livelihood, gathering the exiles, justice, the wicked, the righteous, ירושלים, דוד's kingdom, and hearing prayer. It is one blessing that ends with שומע תפלה. You still say the first three and last three blessings normally.

keyTerms.meaning: "Give us understanding", the name of שמואל's short blessing
Redeemed
Our scattered people
Who hears prayer, the ending of the blessing

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not mean you skip the whole עמידה. הביננו replaces only the thirteen middle blessings. The first three and last three are still said.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
"Give us understanding, Lord our God, to know Your ways,
and soften our hearts to fear You,
phrases.notes: Literally, "circumcise our hearts", meaning remove what blocks our hearts.

phrases.english: and forgive us so that we may be redeemed,
and keep us far from our pains,
and fill us from the pastures of Your land,
and gather our scattered ones from the four corners,
and those who stray will be judged by Your will,
and raise Your hand against the wicked,
and may the righteous rejoice in the building of Your city
and in the restoring of Your Temple,
and in the flourishing strength of David Your servant
and in setting up a lamp for the son of Yishai, Your anointed one,
before we call, may You answer.
phrases.notes: Based on ישעיהו 65:24.

phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: הֲבִינֵנוּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לָדַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 24, different from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One combined blessing, הביננו, takes the place of the thirteen middle blessings.

steps.title: אביי curses those who say הביננו
steps.stepSummary: אביי curses anyone who prays with הביננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי cursed anyone who prays "הביננו".
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows how strongly he opposes using the short הביננו prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמואל gave the wording, אביי did not want people to use it as a shortcut. The text doesn't give his reason here, but the message is clear: do not make a habit of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Cursed
Who prays

phrases.english: Abaye cursed
anyone who prays "Give us understanding."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָיֵיט עֲלַהּ אַבָּיֵי אַמַּאן דִּמְצַלֵּי הֲבִינֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to שמואל's הביננו from step 26 by strongly discouraging it.

steps.title: No הביננו on מוצאי שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: הביננו may be said all year except on מוצאי שבת and מוצאי יום טוב, because הבדלה has to be said in חונן הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: all year long a person may pray הביננו, except on מוצאי שבת and מוצאי יום טוב, because he must say הבדלה in the blessing "Who grants knowledge".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit on when הביננו can be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On מוצאי שבת we add הבדלה (אתה חוננתנו) into the blessing חונן הדעת. הביננו does not include the full חונן הדעת blessing, so there is no place to put הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The night after שבת ends
Marking the separation between holy days and weekdays
The blessing for knowledge, the fourth blessing of the עמידה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
The whole year long
a person may pray "Give us understanding,"

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִמּוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת וּמִמּוֹצָאֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: except for the end of Shabbat and the end of festivals,
because he needs to say havdala
in "Who graciously grants knowledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם הֲבִינֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to שמואל's הביננו from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הביננו may not be used on מוצאי שבת or יום טוב, because הבדלה must go into חונן הדעת.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל: say הבדלה as its own blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל challenges: why not say הבדלה as a separate fourth blessing and then say הביננו? A משנה shows that רבי עקיבא allows exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל objected: let him say הבדלה as a fourth blessing by itself! Didn't we learn in a משנה: רבי עקיבא says he says it as a fourth blessing by itself; רבי אליעזר says it goes in the thanksgiving blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל attacks the rule from step 28. He shows that הבדלה does not have to be inside חונן הדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 assumed that הבדלה can only go in חונן הדעת. But רבי עקיבא says it can be its own fourth blessing, and רבי אליעזר puts it in הודאה. So a person could say the first three blessings, then הבדלה alone, then הביננו, and there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it
By itself, as a separate blessing
Didn't we learn in a משנה?
The thanksgiving blessing (מודים)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel challenged it:
Let him say it as a fourth blessing by itself!
phrases.notes: "It" means הבדלה, said right after the first three blessings.

phrases.english: Didn't we learn in a mishna:
Rabbi Akiva says:
He says it as a fourth blessing by itself.
Rabbi Eliezer says: in the thanksgiving blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְנֵימְרַהּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exception given in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule (step 28) that הביננו cannot be said on מוצאי שבת because of הבדלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule assumes הבדלה must be in חונן הדעת. But a משנה shows רבי עקיבא lets it be a separate fourth blessing, so there would still be a place for הבדלה even with הביננו.

steps.title: The חכמים set seven blessings, not eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea of a separate fourth blessing for הבדלה. We don't follow רבי עקיבא the rest of the year either, because the Sages set a fixed number of blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we follow רבי עקיבא the rest of the year, that we should follow him now? Why don't we follow him the rest of the year? Because the Sages set eighteen blessings, not nineteen. Here too, they set seven, not eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה בר שמואל's challenge from Step 29. A separate הבדלה blessing is not allowed, because the number of blessings is fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's view, that הבדלה is its own blessing, is not the practice even on a normal מוצאי שבת. The reason is that the weekday עמידה has exactly eighteen blessings. In the same way, the short prayer was set at exactly seven, so adding an eighth is not an option.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it so that…? (opens a question that expects the answer 'no')
They instituted (the Sages set it up)
Eighteen
Nineteen

phrases.english: Is it so that throughout the entire year
we act according to Rabbi Akiva,
that now too we should act that way?!
Throughout the entire year, what is the reason
that we do not act according to Rabbi Akiva?

phrases.aramaic: תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי תַּקּוּן, תְּשַׁסְרֵי לָא תַּקּוּן
phrases.english: They instituted eighteen; they did not institute nineteen.
Here too, they instituted seven
phrases.notes: The seven are the first three blessings, הביננו, and the last three.

phrases.english: they did not institute eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר שמואל's challenge from Step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: The halacha does not follow the source cited (רבי עקיבא), and the number of blessings is fixed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הבדלה could be said as a separate fourth blessing, followed by הביננו
steps.terutzMaskana: No extra blessing may be added; the short prayer stays at seven blessings

steps.title: Why not put הבדלה inside הביננו itself?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא suggests weaving הבדלה into the wording of הביננו, which would not add a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: Let him include it in the short blessing itself: 'Grant us understanding, Lord our God, Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary!'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges שמואל's rule that הביננו can't be said on מוצאי שבת. He suggests adding the הבדלה words right into הביננו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem from Step 30 was adding an eighth blessing. מר זוטרא avoids that problem by keeping seven blessings and only adding a few words inside הביננו. So why should הביננו be banned on מוצאי שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it strongly
Let him include it within the general (short) blessing
Who separates between holy and ordinary

phrases.english: Mar Zutra objects to it:
Let him include it within the general blessing:
phrases.notes: He means: fit הבדלה right into the wording of הביננו.

phrases.english: "Grant us understanding, Lord our God,
Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary!"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ מָר זוּטְרָא: וְנִכְלְלָה מִכְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the 'no eighth blessing' rule but finds another way to include הבדלה
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule (Step 28) that הביננו may not be said on מוצאי שבת and מוצאי יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הבדלה can be inserted into הביננו's wording without adding a blessing, so there is no reason to forbid הביננו

steps.title: מר זוטרא's question is left standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has no answer, and the question remains a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to מר זוטרא's question about הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קשיא here means the challenge stays open and nothing is resolved. This matters for the next steps, where the גמרא wonders why an answer it gives about rain wasn't used here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (the question stays unanswered)

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 31 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No answer is given to מר זוטרא's suggestion to include הבדלה inside הביננו

steps.title: הביננו is not said in the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי adds another limit: הביננו is not said in the rainy season, because the request for rain has to go in ברכת השנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: A person may say הביננו all year, except in the rainy season, because he has to say the request for rain in the blessing of the years.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement adds a second time of year when הביננו may not be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like שמואל's rule about מוצאי שבת. In winter we add a request for rain to ברכת השנים. הביננו does not have that full blessing, so it is not said in that season.

keyTerms.meaning: The rainy season (winter)
The request for rain (טל ומטר)
The blessing for a good year and crops

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
Throughout the entire year a person may pray "Grant us understanding,"
except during the rainy season,
because he must say the request
in the blessing of "the years."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exception, like שמואל's מוצאי שבת rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הביננו may not be said in the rainy season, because the request for rain belongs in ברכת השנים

steps.title: Why not put the rain request inside הביננו?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא again suggests adding the needed words into הביננו: 'and give dew and rain'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: Let him include it in the short blessing: 'And satisfy us with the pastures of Your land, and give dew and rain!'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא makes the same kind of challenge he made about הבדלה, now against רב ביבי בר אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הביננו already has a line for ברכת השנים: 'satisfy us with the pastures of Your land'. Adding 'and give dew and rain' there would cover the winter request without dropping הביננו.

keyTerms.meaning: And satisfy us with the pastures of Your land
Dew and rain

phrases.english: Mar Zutra objects to it:
Let him include it within the general blessing:
"And satisfy us with the pastures of Your land,
and give dew and rain!"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ מָר זוּטְרָא: וְנִכְלְלָה מִכְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ביבי בר אביי's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's rule that הביננו isn't said in the rainy season
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rain request can be added inside הביננו's wording, so there is no reason to forbid הביננו

steps.title: He would get confused
steps.stepSummary: Adding a new phrase to the fixed short text would confuse the person praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will come to be confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers מר זוטרא: changing the wording of הביננו would make the person mix up his prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הביננו is a set text that people say by memory. Slipping in a new phrase only in certain seasons is likely to throw the person off. So it is better not to say הביננו in winter at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to be confused or mixed up

phrases.english: He will come to be confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge about rain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Simply add 'dew and rain' inside הביננו
steps.terutzMaskana: A new insertion would confuse the person, so הביננו is not said in winter

steps.title: Then the same answer should work for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: If confusion is a good reason, the גמרא could have used it for הבדלה too. Why did it leave מר זוטרא's first question as קשיא?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, putting הבדלה in 'Who grants knowledge' would also confuse him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns its own answer back on Step 32. It asks why the 'confusion' answer wasn't given for הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding הבדלה into הביננו is the same kind of change as adding rain. So confusion should have answered מר זוטרא's first question, and it should not have been left as an unanswered קשיא. The גמרא now needs to explain how the two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The blessing 'Who graciously grants knowledge', where הבדלה is said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the rule about rain. It asks why the same answer wasn't used earlier for הבדלה, where the גמרא just said קשיא.

phrases.english: If so,
with הבדלה in "Who graciously grants knowledge,"
phrases.notes: Here this means the part of הביננו that stands for חונן הדעת.

phrases.english: he will also come to be confused!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from Step 35 to question why Step 32 was left unanswered
steps.kashyaTarget: The גמרא's leaving מר זוטרא's הבדלה question as קשיא (Step 32)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The confusion answer applies equally to adding הבדלה inside הביננו, so it should have answered the first question too

steps.title: Start of the prayer versus middle of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: Adding הבדלה to הביננו does not confuse the person praying because it comes at the start. Adding the rain request would confuse him because it comes in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: There, since it comes at the beginning of the prayer, he does not get confused. Here, since it comes in the middle of the prayer, he does get confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 36. It explains why confusion is a real worry for the rain request but not for הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why confusion is not also a problem for הבדלה. The answer: הבדלה is added at the very beginning of הביננו, while the mind is still fresh, so it does not throw the person off. The rain request would land in the middle of the fixed short text, and that is where a person loses his place.

keyTerms.meaning: They say; an unnamed answer from the scholars
The beginning of the prayer
The middle of the prayer
Gets confused or mixed up

phrases.english: They say: There, since it comes
phrases.notes: "There" means הבדלה. "Here" in the next part means the rain request.

phrases.english: at the beginning of the prayer, he does not get confused.
Here, since it comes
in the middle of the prayer, he does get confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם כֵּיוָן דְּאָתְיָא בִּתְחִלַּת צְלוֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 36 by showing how הבדלה and the rain request differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (where the added words fall in the prayer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If confusion is a concern, it should block adding הבדלה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Confusion only happens when words are added in the middle. הבדלה is added at the start, so it is fine.

steps.title: Why not ask for rain in שומע תפלה?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests putting the rain request in the שומע תפלה part, at the end of הביננו. He proves from רבי תנחום in the name of רב אסי that שומע תפלה is a valid place for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: Let him say it in שומע תפלה! For רבי תנחום said in the name of רב אסי: If someone made a mistake and did not mention the power of rain in תחיית המתים, we make him go back. If he forgot the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we do not make him go back, because he can say it in שומע תפלה. If he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not make him go back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the last answer. He says the rain request could go at the end of הביננו, in שומע תפלה, where it would not cause confusion in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer said the problem was adding words in the middle. But רב אסי teaches that someone who forgot the rain request may say it in שומע תפלה. So it could be added at the end of הביננו, where there is no confusion, and הביננו should be allowed in the rainy season.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it strongly
The blessing 'Who hears prayer,' where personal requests may be added
Praising ה׳'s power of rain (מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם)
We make him go back and say it again
The blessing 'Who grants knowledge' (אַתָּה חוֹנֵן)
Over the cup of wine (הבדלה after davening)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different things. 'Mentioning' rain (מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ) is praise in the second blessing. 'Asking' for rain (וְתֵן טַל וּמָטָר) is a request in ברכת השנים.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged it:
Let him say it in "Who hears prayer"!
phrases.notes: "It" is the rain request. הביננו ends with the theme of שומע תפלה, so he could add it there.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אסי shows the rain request may be said in שומע תפלה, which comes at the end of הביננו, so there is no confusion.

steps.title: Only someone who made a mistake may use שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The option of asking for rain in שומע תפלה applies only to someone who forgot. You may not plan from the start to put it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who made a mistake is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי in two words: רב אסי's rule is only a backup for someone who already made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי was not saying שומע תפלה is a regular place for the rain request. He was saying that if someone already forgot, he can fix it there. A person saying הביננו would be planning from the start to skip ברכת השנים, and that is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a mistake
Is different
From the start, as the planned way to act

steps.whatToRemember: A fix for a mistake (בדיעבד) is not a plan you may choose from the start (לכתחילה). This is why the rain request still blocks הביננו in the rainy season.

phrases.english: One who made a mistake is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge by limiting רב אסי's rule to someone who forgot.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the rain request works in שומע תפלה, it may be added at the end of הביננו.
steps.terutzMaskana: שומע תפלה works only for someone who forgot. You cannot plan to use it, so הביננו stays off-limits in the rainy season.

steps.title: Looking at רב אסי's teaching on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes רבי תנחום's teaching in the name of רב אסי by itself, so it can examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The teaching itself: רבי תנחום said in the name of רב אסי: If someone made a mistake and did not mention the power of rain in תחיית המתים, we make him go back. If he forgot the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we do not make him go back, because he can say it in שומע תפלה. If he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not make him go back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new discussion. It repeats רב אסי's teaching, which it just quoted in passing, so it can now examine it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the teaching was only used as a tool in רב אשי's question. The word גופא tells us the גמרא is now turning to the teaching itself. It lists three cases: forgetting the mention of rain means going back, while forgetting the rain request or הבדלה does not, because each has another place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': the גמרא returns to examine a teaching it quoted earlier
The second blessing of שמונה עשרה, about reviving the dead
The ninth blessing, asking for a good year, where we ask for rain

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting the mention of rain means going back. Forgetting the rain request or הבדלה does not, because each can be said somewhere else (שומע תפלה or over the cup).

steps.title: A ברייתא says the forgotten rain request does require going back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same three cases. It disagrees with רב אסי on the middle case: someone who forgot the rain request must go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged it from a ברייתא: If someone made a mistake and did not mention the power of rain in תחיית המתים, we make him go back. If he forgot the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we make him go back. If he forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not make him go back, because he can say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's teaching from a ברייתא. On the rain request, the ברייתא says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רב אסי about mentioning rain and about הבדלה. The only difference is the rain request: the ברייתא says he must go back, and it does not mention a backup in שומע תפלה. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רב אסי, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged it (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
The request for rain (וְתֵן טַל וּמָטָר), as opposed to only mentioning it

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that someone who forgot the rain request in ברכת השנים does not go back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא with the same three cases rules that he does go back, which contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: First answer: one source is about an individual, the other about a congregation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the ברייתא (go back) is about a יחיד, and רב אסי (no need to go back) is about someone praying in a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about an individual, and that one is about a congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to solve the contradiction from Step 41 by saying the two sources are talking about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא, which says he must go back, is about a person praying alone. רב אסי, who says he does not go back, is about a person praying with a ציבור. This way the two sources do not argue at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The opening words of an answer that splits two sources into different cases
An individual praying alone
A congregation, a group praying together

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This is about an individual,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא, which says he must go back.

phrases.english: that is about a congregation.
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי, who says he does not need to go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּיָחִיד, הָא בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 41 between the ברייתא and רב אסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רב אסי seem to argue about the same person who forgot the rain request.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a יחיד, and רב אסי is about someone praying in a ציבור.

steps.title: Rejecting the answer: רב אסי's reason does not fit a congregation
steps.stepSummary: If the congregation case does not go back because he hears the שליח ציבור, then רב אסי should have given that reason. Instead he said it was because he can ask in שומע תפלה, so the first answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a congregation, why does he not go back? Because he hears it from the שליח ציבור. If so, instead of saying 'because he can say it in שומע תפלה,' he should have said 'because he hears it from the שליח ציבור.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer from Step 42 and shows it does not match the reason רב אסי actually gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason a person in a ציבור would not need to go back is that he hears the rain request when the שליח ציבור repeats the עמידה. But רב אסי's reason was that he can still add it in שומע תפלה, a reason that fits anyone, even someone praying alone. So רב אסי's case cannot be limited to a ציבור, and the answer is pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The prayer leader who repeats the עמידה out loud for the congregation
If so. Introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
He should have said. The wording should have been different

phrases.english: With a congregation, what is the reason he does not go back?
Because he hears it from the prayer leader.
If so, this statement,
'because he can say it in "Who hears prayer,"'
phrases.notes: These are רב אסי's own words from Step 40.

phrases.english: should have said: 'because he hears it from the prayer leader.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַאי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְאוֹמְרָהּ בְּשׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִילָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵעַ מִשְּׁלִיחַ צִיבּוּר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the יחיד/ציבור answer from Step 42.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole answer that splits the sources into יחיד and ציבור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אסי's stated reason (he can say it in שומע תפלה) does not match the reason a ציבור case would need (he hears the שליח ציבור).

steps.title: New answer: both are about an individual, and it depends on when he remembers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new answer. Both sources are about a יחיד. רב אסי (no going back) is about someone who remembered before reaching שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are about an individual, and it is not difficult: this one is where he remembered before 'Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first answer, the גמרא starts a different answer. Only the first half appears here; the other half of the split comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the difference is not who is praying but when he notices his mistake. If he remembers before he reaches שומע תפלה, he can still add the rain request there, so he does not go back. This fits רב אסי's own reason exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the earlier answer and brings a new one
Both this and that, both sources
He remembered
The ברכה 'Who hears prayer,' the last request ברכה of the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not finished yet. Here we only hear the case where he does not go back (remembered before שומע תפלה). The case where he must go back comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are about an individual,
and it is not difficult:
this is where he remembered before 'Who hears prayer,'
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי's case: he can still ask for rain in שומע תפלה, so he does not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּיָחִיד, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 43 with a new way to solve the contradiction from Step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by timing: when he remembers his mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first answer split the sources by individual versus congregation, but that did not fit רב אסי's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources are about a יחיד. רב אסי is about someone who remembered before שומע תפלה (the other case continues in the next line).
